The presence of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates and admixed plasma cells could suggest a reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, but the atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement indicate a more neoplastic process.

The negative immunohistochemical staining for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56, along with the presence of atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, points towards Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
